evidence.quote: EDS analysis indicated that the thin plate precipitates contain Ti Al, Sc. The stoichiometric ratio of Ti and (Al +Sc) is about 3:1, suggesting that the precipitates should be Ti 3(Al, Sc).
after compression deformation, lamellar near eutectoid structure boundary were bent and some equiaxial grains with the size of about 0.3 mm occurred in front of bent lamellar structure

attributes.location: in front of bent lamellar structure

mechanisms.name: precipitate obstacle to interlamellar sliding and dislocation slipping

evidence.quote: The obstacle to interlamellar sliding and dislocation slipping caused by Ti 3(Al, Sc) precipitates should be responsible for yield strength increment of Ti–Al alloys with Sc.

conflicts.description: Reported yield strength increment from Sc addition is inconsistent: abstract states 120 and 125 MPa for Ti-Al and Ti-48Al respectively, while results and conclusions state 110 MPa.

evidence.quote: the yield strength increment is 120 and 125 MPa, respectively
Adding of 0.4% Sc to Ti–Al and Ti–48Al base alloys can remarkably increase their high temperature yield strength. The strength increment reached 110 MPa.
